StringWithMarkup.String: Progressive cirrhosis of the lungs was found in a subchronic inhalation study in rats. Rats were exposed intermittently for 6-9 months to an inert aerosol (control), to the inert aerosol enriched with 1OX or 49% insoluble thorium dioxide, or to thorium dioxide (100%) alone. The severity of the lung cirrhosis was directly related to the radiation dose and the amount of thorium dioxide. Cirrhosis of the lungs became evident in 3-6 months in the 100% thorium dioxide group, in 9-12 months in the 49% thorium dioxide group, in 12-15 months in the 10% thorium dioxide group, and in 18-24 months in the inert aerosol control group.
